d: One command installs the fleetd CLI, plus the desktop app on a machine with a display.
x: curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh Then set it up: Quick start . Platforms CLI (hub and workers) Desktop app Linux x64 yes yes macOS, Apple silicon yes yes macOS, Intel yes yes The hub also needs git , and the claude and gh CLIs logged in to your own accounts. A worker needs only claude . fleetd init checks each one and prints the install command for anything missing. What it installs The CLI at ~/.fleetd/bin/fleetd , linked from ~/.local/bin/fleetd . The desktop app, on macOS and on Linux with a display: ~/Applications/fleetd.app , or ~/.local/share/fleetd/app with a menu entry. Every download is checked against the release's SHA256SUMS . The installer needs no sudo and starts no services: fleetd init does that. Running it again replaces what it installed. To read it first, open fleetd.sh/install.sh . Options curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --app # the app too, on Linux without a display curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --no-app # the CLI only curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --app Releases are nightly builds for now. FLEETD_CHANNEL=stable picks the stable channel once it has a release. Verify fleetd version If your shell can't find fleetd , add ~/.local/bin to your PATH , or run ~/.local/bin/fleetd .

d: Install, set up the hub and send a first order in three steps.
x: Run steps 1 and 2 on the always-on machine that will be your hub. Step 3 is on the computer you work from. 1. Install fleetd curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh 2. Set it up Run fleetd init . It asks a few questions (Enter takes the default) and ticks off each step. A ✗ line ends with the command that fixes it. Run it again at any time: it keeps what works and repairs the rest. fleetd init fleetd init asks where the hub listens: your tailnet first when it finds Tailscale, then this machine only, then your LAN: It never opens the hub to the internet. 3. Send your first order On the computer you work from, install fleetd with its app and open it: curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --app open ~/Applications/fleetd.app # macOS ~/.local/share/fleetd/app/fleetd-app & # Linux (or "fleetd" in your app menu) Enter the hub address and the pairing code fleetd init printed. Codes last 15 minutes; fleetd pair on the hub prints a new one. Then press ⌘N (Ctrl+N on Linux) and type an order, such as fix the typo in the README . The order starts the project's lead, which answers with a brief and starts work. Its questions land in the inbox. Next: Concepts , or more machines .

d: The hub, nodes, leads, orders, asks and the merge train, one short section each.
x: Hub One per fleet, on an always-on machine ( fleetd hub start , run as a service by fleetd init ). It holds everything that lasts: projects, leads, briefs, tasks, asks and decisions, the merge train, checks and wakes. It serves the desktop app and one MCP endpoint, <hub url>/mcp , over all your machines. Its data is one SQLite file in ~/.fleetd/hub . Nodes One fleetd node per machine that runs agents (a worker). The node dials out to the hub, so no worker opens a port. It runs one claude process per live session, each writer in its own git worktree and branch. Sessions use your own claude setup in ~/.claude : the same login, proxy settings and MCP servers as the claude in your shell. The hub machine is usually a worker too. Leads Each project has one lead: a long-running claude session that turns orders into briefs, splits them into tasks for writer and reviewer sessions, and never writes code itself. Leads run on claude-opus-5-5 by default. A project's first order starts its lead. Orders An order is one line of intent, such as fix the typo in the README , sent from the app or with intake_submit over MCP. The hub picks the project (a leading @project names it), opens a workstream and wakes the lead. The lead freezes a brief with done-when checks, then spawns tasks. A slot board caps how many sessions run at once. Asks and decisions A lead asks you only about product calls, money, credentials and irreversible steps. Asks arrive numbered, in batches, in the app's inbox; you answer tersely ( 1 go 2 nvm 3 b ). Each answer becomes a decision in a searchable log, and an ask that a past decision already answers comes back at once without bothering you. Some asks need more than words: approving an exact command, ticking off steps, or entering a secret. See Approvals & secrets . Merge train Only fleetd merges. Each writer's PR goes on its repo's train, one serial queue per repo. The train rebases each ready change onto its base, waits for CI on that exact head and squash-merges it. A change's tier sets its reviews: S needs none, M one clean review, L two plus a verifier, each bound to the current patch. A PR body needs a Source: line naming what it serves. You can freeze a repo's train with train_freeze . Done, checked A lead can't just say "done". fleetd claim done makes the hub run the workstream's done-when checks itself (a PR merged, CI green, a command or test on a machine, an HTTP check, a judge, a person), and only all of them passing makes it done. Each claim keeps its evidence and exit codes.

d: Add workers to the hub, log in their Claude, remove them, and check their health.
h: Add a machine the hub can reach over SSH
Add a machine the hub can't reach
x: A worker is any machine that runs agents. It needs the claude CLI, and for now the same OS and CPU as the hub. Run these on the hub. Add a machine the hub can reach over SSH Run fleetd init again and pick it from the list (hosts from ~/.ssh/config and your tailnet), or name it: fleetd machine add homeserver It copies the hub's own fleetd there, enrolls the node with a one-time token, runs it as a user service and waits until the machine is online. It prints every remote command before it runs it. --dry-run only prints the plan: fleetd machine add builder-1 --dry-run It is safe to run again: a real run reads the machine's state first and skips what is done. Add this machine fleetd machine add --local The same steps, run here without SSH. Use it to make the hub machine a worker too, or to repair it. fleetd init does this when you pick "(this machine)". Add a machine the hub can't reach For a laptop behind NAT, or anything without SSH from the hub, print a one-line join command on the hub and paste it on the new machine: fleetd pair --worker laptop The code lasts 15 minutes. The machine must reach the hub's address. Run the command again later to repair the worker; --rejoin enrolls it again with a new code. Claude on a worker Sessions use the worker's own claude setup ( ~/.claude ), so if claude works in your shell there, it works for fleetd: your login, a proxy set in ~/.claude/settings.json and your MCP servers included. If it is not logged in, log in as you normally do: claude auth login Behind a proxy, log in with your proxy instead. fleetd doctor shows each worker's claude, login and proxy. See The Claude login for a dedicated profile per machine. Remove a machine fleetd machine remove homeserver It stops and removes the node's service there and revokes its key on the hub. --purge also deletes ~/.fleetd/node and ~/.fleetd/claude.env on that machine; your own ~/.claude stays. For a machine that joined with pair --worker , only the key is revoked; stop its node there yourself: fleetd machine remove laptop Check health fleetd doctor It checks the hub and every machine (online, claude version and login, commit identity, disk, usage breaker) and prints the fix for each problem. The app's Machines screen shows the same checks. Every finding and its fix: Troubleshooting .

d: Add a project, send an order, follow it, and see how "done" is checked.
x: Add a project Run fleetd init again and pick a repo: a checkout it finds on a worker, or a GitHub URL, which it clones. The rest of your setup stays as it is. From an MCP client, project_add {machineId, path, title} adds one and project_remove {machineId, projectId} forgets it (its files, branches and worktrees stay). Its lead Each project has one lead, and the project's first order starts it: there is nothing to start by hand. The lead's first message lists the order, and the app shows the lead starting. If the lead can't start, because claude on the worker is logged out or outside the supported version range, or the worker is offline, the order waits. The app's reply says why and what to run on the worker. Once the worker comes back online with a usable claude , its lead starts and picks up every waiting order. To choose the lead's model and effort, or to start it before any order, call lead_start {machineId, projectId, model, effort} from an MCP client; the model and effort are saved for the project (default claude-opus-5-5 , high). To keep a project's lead from starting by itself, set lead.autoStart: false in its policy file : orders then wait until lead_start , and the reply says so. Connect an MCP client The hub's MCP endpoint is <hub url>/mcp . Give the client an agent key, shown once: fleetd hub key create --name ci-bot --role operate --machines '*' For Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http fleetd http://hub.your-tailnet.ts.net:4790/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer fld_<key>" Roles are read , operate and admin , on every machine ( '*' ) or a list. fleetd hub key list shows keys and fleetd hub key revoke <keyId> ends one at once. Send an order In the app, press ⌘N (Ctrl+N), type one line and press Enter. Aim it at a project, or leave it to the hub, which reads a leading @project , else asks a quick router, else asks you. A prefix picks the playbook: fix: or bug: , research: , finish: . From an MCP client: intake_submit {text} . Follow it The lead freezes a brief, runs writer and reviewer tasks on your workers, and puts each PR on the merge train. Follow it on the app's Projects screen (⌘2), or with workstream_list , workstream_get , thread_tail and fleetd_status . events_wait long-polls for changes instead of polling. Answer its questions Questions land in the inbox (⌘1), numbered. Reply in one line, such as 1 go 2 nvm 3 b : see the reply grammar . Commands and secrets have their own flow: Approvals & secrets . Done, checked The lead reports done with fleetd claim done . The hub then runs the brief's done-when checks itself, and only all of them passing makes the workstream done. A failure wakes the lead with the exit code and output. claims_list shows every claim with its evidence.

d: The asks only a person answers, from the desktop app: commands, tool prompts, checklists and secrets.
x: These asks come to the inbox like any other, but only a person's device answers them (a human key, which the app holds). An agent key can't, and "recs fine" or "all go" never answers them in bulk. Approve a command When a lead needs an irreversible, money or credential step, it files the exact command with fleetd gated run . You see the command, the reason and where it runs. Reply <n> go to run it or <n> no to refuse. The node runs exactly the stored bytes, in the project's workspace, and the exit code and output go back to the lead. Tool permission prompts Leads and tasks run with claude's permission prompts off. A session started with thread_launch and runtimeMode: approval-required sends each prompt to you as an approve ask instead. A prompt that stays open is raised again after 10 minutes, then every 30. A project can answer prompts itself with rules in claude's own syntax in .fleetd/policy.yaml : tools: allow: ["Bash(npm test:*)", "Read"] deny: ["Bash(git push:*)"] A deny rule wins over an allow rule. Rules apply to every session in the project; see Config & files . Checklists Some steps only you can do, such as clicking through a provider's console. The lead files them as a checklist ask ( fleetd ask --kind do ). Reply <n> done once you've done them. If the ask has a check, the hub runs it, and a failure reopens the ask with the evidence. Secrets When a lead needs an API key or password, it files a secret ask that names the machine and where the value goes (an env file line or a file). Type the value in the app. The app seals it to that machine's key (a libsodium sealed box) and wipes what you typed. The hub relays the ciphertext without storing it, the node writes it (mode 0600), and the lead only ever sees its fingerprint. The target machine must be online: nothing is queued. A gated command can use a stored secret as an environment variable ( --secret-env ); the node reads it from its own files.

d: Pair the app with your hub, answer the inbox in one line, and the keyboard shortcuts.
x: The app is where you send orders, answer asks, approve commands and enter secrets. Install it with curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --app ( Install ). Pair it with the hub On the hub machine the app pairs by itself. On another computer, print a code on the hub: fleetd pair Enter the address and code on the app's "Connect to your fleetd hub" screen, or open the fleetd://pair link. The code works once, for 15 minutes. The app keeps its key in the OS keychain, never in a file. Settings (⌘,) shows the hub it is paired with and disconnects it; "Connect to a hub…" in the palette pairs with another. Inbox and replies The inbox (⌘1) lists what needs you, in numbered batches. Answer a whole batch in one line in the reply box at the bottom of every screen. Typing anywhere outside a field goes there. Reply Means 1 go accept item 1 (also yes , y , ok , rec ) 2 nvm reject item 2 (also no , drop , skip , n ) 3 b pick option b of item 3 ( a to f ) 1-3 go the same answer for items 1 to 3 2: use the staging bucket answer in your own words 4 later not now; it stays open 5 done you did a checklist's steps recs fine accept every recommendation not mentioned #B4 1 go answer batch 4, not the latest pref: no new dependencies a standing preference for every lead forget D12 drop decision 12 Mix them: 1 go 2 nvm 3 b . A reply the app can't read changes nothing and shows a hint. Up in the empty reply box recalls what you sent before. Asks that block work also raise a desktop notification: at most one every 20 minutes, with the rest folded in as "+N more", and only urgent ones in quiet hours (23:00 to 08:00 unless a policy.quiet_hours decision says otherwise). Shortcuts ⌘ on macOS is Ctrl on Linux. Keys Does ⌘K Command palette: every project, thread, open ask and action ⌘N New order ⌘1 / ⌘2 / ⌘3 Inbox / Projects / Machines ⌘, Settings ⌘B Toggle the sidebar ↑ ↓ Move the selection in a list or the palette (also Ctrl+P / Ctrl+N in the palette) Enter Open the selected project, run the palette item, or send Shift+Enter New line in a reply or order Esc Clear the field, close a dialog, or go back to Projects Tab / Shift+Tab Next / previous control ⌘Q Quit ⌃⌘F (macOS), F11 (Linux) Full screen ⌘H, ⌥⌘H, ⌘M (macOS) Hide, hide others, minimize Text fields follow the usual editing keys of each platform (word motion, undo and redo, select all).

d: Where fleetd keeps its state, the Claude login it uses, the project policy file, and its port.
x: ~/.fleetd fleetd uninstall keeps all of it; see Updating & uninstall . The Claude login Sessions run claude with your own setup on that machine: ~/.claude (or the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR the node's service has), so your login, the env in ~/.claude/settings.json (a proxy's ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL , say), an apiKeyHelper and your MCP servers work as they do in your shell. If claude works for you on the worker, it works for fleetd. Otherwise log in as you normally do: claude auth login , or through your proxy. fleetd doctor shows what each worker uses, e.g. claude 2.1.302, logged in (Max), via proxy http://127.0.0.1:8317 from ~/.claude/settings.json . fleetd adds its own settings per session on top of yours, never in their place: an --mcp-config for its servers and a --settings overlay that pins claude's version and denies the tools agents never get (subagents, plan mode, worktrees, cron). To give a worker's sessions a dedicated claude profile instead, set "claudeConfigDir": "<dir>" in ~/.fleetd/node/node.json (or join with fleetd node join --claude-config-dir <dir> ) and restart the node. A session resumes only under the config dir it started in; the node refuses a resume under another one and says so. The hub's own claude (the order router and the retro) uses your normal login on the hub machine ( ~/.claude ), or the gateway variables in claude.env . claude.env Optional. KEY=VALUE lines for the claude that fleetd runs, for a variable your login needs that the services don't see, such as one only your interactive shell exports. Blank lines, # comments and export are allowed. Mode 0600. Your ~/.claude/settings.json env outranks it, as it does for your own claude . CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<token from claude setup-token> # or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example.com ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<token> Nodes add every line to each session's environment and re-read the file at each start. The hub service loads the file when it starts, so restart it after a change. Its own claude gets only ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL , ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from it. A CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN there reaches the node's sessions but not the hub's router. fleetd init offers to copy these from your shell when it finds them there. .fleetd/policy.yaml An optional file in a project's repo; commit it to the default branch. Changes apply within a minute. Without it, writers may touch the whole repo. areas: # what a writer task may touch; a task leases one or more areas docs: ["docs/**"] app: ["src/**", "package.json"] defaults: # optional: the project's task model and effort (low, medium, high, max) model: claude-opus-5-5 effort: high finishAll: # optional maxChildren: 10 # most child workstreams one finish-all run starts tools: # optional: claude permission rules for every session allow: ["Bash(npm test:*)"] deny: ["Bash(git push:*)"] lead: # optional autoStart: false # orders wait for lead_start instead of starting the lead (default true) Area names are lowercase slugs. A broken file is refused with the exact problem, never ignored, so a typo can't widen what a writer may touch. Services fleetd init and fleetd machine add run the hub and node as user services: Linux (systemd) macOS (launchd) Hub ~/.config/systemd/user/fleetd-hub.service ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.fleetd.hub.plist Node ~/.config/systemd/user/fleetd-node.service ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.fleetd.node.plist --unit-suffix <s> adds a suffix to these names, for a second fleet on one machine. Ports and addresses The hub listens on one port, 4790 by default: on your tailnet address when fleetd init finds Tailscale, otherwise on 127.0.0.1 only. The desktop app, nodes and MCP clients all use it ( <hub url>/mcp for MCP). Workers open no port: their nodes dial out. Change it with fleetd init --listen <host:port> --url <url> . The app The app's pairing hand-off from fleetd init or fleetd pair on the same machine is ~/.config/fleetd/app-pair.json (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/fleetd/app-pair.json ). Its hub key is in the OS keychain.

d: What fleetd trusts, how keys and secrets move, and how to report a vulnerability.
x: fleetd is built for one person or a small team running their own fleet. Network The hub is never public by default. fleetd init listens on your tailnet address, or on 127.0.0.1 without Tailscale. Plain HTTP is accepted only there (Tailscale's tunnel is encrypted); anywhere else, put HTTPS in front ( the https check ). Nodes dial out. A worker's node connects to the hub and proves itself with its own key pair, so no worker opens a port. Enrollment tokens and pairing codes work once and expire after 15 minutes. Keys Agent keys are hashed. A fld_ key is shown once; the hub stores only its hash and prefix. Each key has read, operate or admin rights on every machine or a named list. A revoked key stops on its next request. A person's device holds a human key , in the OS keychain, never in a file. Only human keys answer secret, approve and checklist asks, so no agent can approve itself. The node socket trusts the node's OS user. Lead-side commands reach the hub through ~/.fleetd/node/node.sock (mode 0600), and the hub attributes each call to the project whose workspace contains the caller's working directory. Any process running as that user can act as any project's lead on that machine. Run agents you don't trust as a different user. Secrets and commands Secrets never reach the hub in plain text. The app seals each value to the target node's key (a libsodium sealed box) and wipes what was typed. The hub relays the ciphertext without storing it and keeps only the fingerprint the node reports. Notifications carry a one-line summary, never a secret. An approved command runs exactly as stored , and only after a person approves it. Webhooks are signed with a Standard Webhooks signature; each subscription's secret is shown once and stored encrypted. Software Installs are checksummed. The installer and fleetd update refuse any release file whose SHA-256 doesn't match the release's SHA256SUMS . fleetd machine add copies the hub's own binary to a worker over SSH. Models only through the claude CLI , with the machine user's own claude setup (their login, settings and MCP servers), so agents get the same Claude access as that user. fleetd never calls a model or usage API itself. Report a vulnerability Privately, through GitHub's security advisories for unlaboredlabs/fleetd .

Each section here is one check: a hub check hub/<name> is #hub-<name> , a machine check <machine>/<name> is #<name> . fleetd doctor ✗ is a failure; ! is a warning or a check that couldn't tell. The hub doesn't answer fleetd doctor Run fleetd init . If you run the hub yourself ( --no-service ), start it with fleetd hub start . The log is ~/.fleetd/hub/hub.log . Not installed: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash The hub isn't reachable over HTTPS The hub's address http://… is not HTTPS; keys from the desktop app and other machines would cross the network unencrypted. Plain HTTP passes on loopback and on a tailnet address ( 100.64.0.0/10 or a *.ts.net name). d: Update fleetd and its app, pick a release channel, and remove fleetd from a machine.
x: Update fleetd update --check fleetd update It replaces the CLI, and the desktop app when the installer put it in its usual place, then restarts the hub and node services that run this binary. Every file is checked against the release's SHA256SUMS . Workers don't update themselves. Update the hub first, then each worker: run fleetd update there, or fleetd machine add <ssh-host> on the hub, which copies the hub's binary over. fleetd pins claude separately: see claude version . Channels fleetd update stays on the channel you installed from. Releases are nightly builds for now; a stable channel comes with the first release. fleetd update --channel stable curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | FLEETD_CHANNEL=stable sh Remove a machine From the hub: fleetd machine remove <id> , with --purge to delete its data too. See Machines . Uninstall the hub fleetd uninstall It stops and removes the hub's service (here there was none) and keeps its data. --purge also deletes ~/.fleetd/hub ; stop a hub you run yourself first. Remove each worker before you purge the hub. Remove the CLI and app curl -fsSL https://fleetd.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall It runs fleetd uninstall first, then removes the CLI and the app. ~/.fleetd stays.
